text.id: First was the "2D-Only" approach, which flattened the brain slices. Second was the "3D-Only" volumetric pipeline, which preserved the complex spatial depth of the MRI. Finally, a complex "Trimodal" fusion method was built to see if combining different data perspectives could create a super-predictor.

text.id: The core question of the thesis: what is the best way to feed a human brain into a neural network? To find out, the study engineered and tested three distinct data processing pipelines.

text.id: To push the limits, these models were tested across two distinct environments. "Version 1" (V1) served as the raw, unfiltered baseline. "Version 2" (V2) was a highly engineered, aggressively enhanced setup that utilized advanced high-pass filtering, spatial attention mechanisms, and radiomic feature extraction to try and force the AI to see more.

text.id: It was a clash of architectures. The research pitted industry-heavyweight networks against each otherâ€”specifically ResNet, EfficientNet, and the highly hyped Vision Transformer (ViT).
